events.credibility_reason: The Woodall case rests on a reported personal communication from Suyama. The paper itself was not read, and the only other source, an unopened snippet, hedges the claim.

why: The statement asks only whether infinitely many base-2 Woodall primes exist, and no event touches that question. The density-zero claim (almost all Woodall numbers composite) cannot decide infinitude, so it answers a different question and is a variant. It is also a pre-snapshot event. The membership results for Fibonacci, Perrin and Padovan sequences are variants. The two prime finds in base 69 (a Cullen prime) and base 355 are different families or bases, so they are variants. The 2018 record prime is one more finite instance and leaves infinitude untouched. Bravo–Irmak is dated only to 2024, so it gets a null date. The record names no AI system for any event.
doubts: The AlphaProof Nexus appendix listing 44 settled OEIS conjectures was not read. A Woodall-related entry there cannot be ruled out, though nothing in the text that was read suggests one.
